memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'He must not eat anything found dead or torn by wild animals, and so
become unclean through it. I am the LORD. The priests are to perform
my service in such a way that they do not become guilty and die for
treating it with contempt. I am the LORD, who makes them holy'"
- Lev 22:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A dead animal found in a field was free food. No cost, no effort. But
the priest was not to touch it. Availability was never the same thing
as permission.

We live in a world that constantly confuses those two. If something is
accessible, affordable and legal, we assume it must be fine. Our
phones put almost anything within reach in seconds. The question our
culture asks is "can I?" The question Scripture asks is "should I?"

Paul put it plainly: I have the right to do anything, but not
everything is beneficial (1 Cor 10:23). Freedom in Christ was never
meant to be an excuse for indulging whatever is within reach (Gal
5:13).

Dear friend, this is not about making a long list of forbidden things.
It is about learning to pause. That pause - that half-second where you
ask God rather than simply reaching - is where much of Christian
maturity is formed.

And notice again the closing words: "I am the LORD, who makes them
holy." Even our self-control is not self-manufactured. The grace of God
teaches us to say no (Titus 2:11-12). Ask Him for that grace today.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where am I confusing "available" with "allowed"?
2. What would it look like to pause and ask God before reaching?
3. Am I relying on willpower or on God's grace for self-control?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, teach me to ask not just what I can do but what I should do.
Give me grace to say no to what harms me and yes to what honours You.
Amen.
